items.description: Read the full requirements and Appendix A; identify every mandatory section, diagram, and formatting rule; create the team outline.
Research OpenPilot's purpose, problems, features, hardware and vehicle interfaces, limitations, and autonomy boundary.
items.expectedOutput: Research notes covering functionality and limitations.

items.description: Write the introduction covering description, motivation, functionality, objectives, scope, and report organization.
After receiving the other sections, write the abstract covering purpose, subsystems, interactions, findings, and conclusions.
Integrate all sections, diagrams, and references; review completeness, terminology, labels, citations, duplication, focus, and page count.
Create and verify the final PDF, publish it on the Group H site, test its links, and complete submission.
items.expectedOutput: Verified publication link and submitted report.

items.description: Study how OpenPilot organizes functionality into current processes and modules.
items.expectedOutput: Source-backed architecture notes and process inventory.

items.description: Identify major subsystems and document each purpose, inputs, outputs, interactions, dependencies, and reason for separation.
items.expectedOutput: Subsystem inventory table with responsibilities, inputs, outputs, dependencies, and references.

items.description: Analyze evidence for modular, message-based, publish-subscribe, pipeline, and layered architectural styles.
Create a labeled overall architecture diagram of the major subsystems and meaningful relationships.
items.expectedOutput: Architecture diagram in SVG or PNG format.

items.description: Create a dependency diagram with clear directions and a legend; keep dependencies distinct from data flow.
items.expectedOutput: Dependency diagram in SVG or PNG format with legend.

items.description: Write the section explaining subsystems, responsibilities, interactions, styles, dependencies, strengths, and limitations.
items.expectedOutput: Referenced 2–3 page section plus both diagrams.

items.description: Study OpenPilot communication mechanisms and messages using current process, controls, planning, and process-replay sources.
items.expectedOutput: Source-backed notes on processes, messages, publishers, and subscribers.

items.description: Trace an adaptive cruise control scenario through observations, perception, planning, controls, vehicle commands, and feedback.
items.expectedOutput: Documented end-to-end data flow using actual components and messages.

items.description: Explain startup, process activation, engagement, command communication, disengagement, and unavailable-information behavior.
Analyze concurrent processes, overlapping activities, message coordination, timing value, and conceptual handling of delayed or invalid inputs.
Create sequence diagram 1 for adaptive cruise control responding to a slower vehicle using verified components and communication relationships.
items.expectedOutput: Sequence diagram in SVG or PNG format.

items.description: Write the section explaining data flow, control flow, concurrency, the sequence diagram, and architectural implications.
items.expectedOutput: Referenced 2–3 page analysis and sequence diagram.

items.description: Study driver, vehicle, camera, sensor, communication-network, alert, and display interfaces.
For each external interface, document the actor, incoming and outgoing information, responsible component, and use of the information.
Analyze lane centering, adaptive cruise control, and driver monitoring with actor, preconditions, trigger, main flow, alternatives, result, and subsystems.
Create sequence or state diagram 2 for a distracted driver, using verified monitoring, self-driving, alert, and UI responsibilities and messages.
Write the section explaining external interfaces, all three use cases, and the driver-monitoring diagram.
items.expectedOutput: Referenced 2–3 page section, interface table, use cases, and diagram.

items.description: Review the architecture, flow, and interface work from Spence, Mehdi, and David; identify important design decisions.
Analyze process separation, messaging, performance, reliability, maintainability, extensibility, safety boundaries, and multi-vehicle support.
items.expectedOutput: Architectural trade-off analysis with benefits, challenges, and implications.

items.description: Explain developer responsibility areas and the coordination needed across shared interfaces without inventing OpenPilot's team structure.
Verify and document modelV2, carState, carControl, longitudinalPlan, driverMonitoringState, selfdriveState, controlsState, radarState, CAN, and panda.
items.expectedOutput: Data dictionary with Term, Type or Category, Meaning, and Used By columns.

items.description: Explain process names, names ending in d, module names, message names, data-structure names, and important abbreviations.
Use process-replay and safety sources to explain how testing and safety mechanisms support the architecture.
Write lessons learned and conclusions covering strengths, limitations, research challenges, improvements, and future directions.
Collect, deduplicate, verify, and consistently format references from every member.

submissionChecklist.label: At least two sequence or state diagrams included
Report formatted to 10–15 pages, single-spaced, 12-point font
